newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lacklustre Australian stocks limp to flat finish.
newsitem.headline: Lacklustre Australian stocks limp to flat finish.

text.p: *Stocks end flat, lanquishing in choppy trade as market nears top of range, eye on results. Volume 358.35 million, A$854.35 million value, 1,115 stocks traded, 335 steady, 401 up, 382 down.
A lacklustre Australian share market limped to a flat finish on Thursday with a bullish streak on Wall Street ignored in favour of a wary eye on the upcoming profit season.
The All Ordinaries index inched up 0.1 points to 2,735.1, swinging around square all day and but never venturing more than eight points either way.
September share price index futures were down 12 points to 2,747, an 11.9 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the market seemed content to churn near the top of its record breaking 1997 range.

"There has been a slowdown in the order flow a bit and I suppose that's because the market is where it is," said director of institutions at Ord Minnett, Eric Gale. "It is still holding the high ground pretty much, it's not too far from an absolute top, but people are struggling to find value (at these levels)."
After yesterday's interest rate reduction, the next key influence was likely to be the flood of June 30 profit reports washing through the market over the next six weeks.
Some concerns still lingered about expectations from this data with traders suggesting some caution was appropriate.
"I hope the market is not demanding more than is possible, in some cases I think they may be," said Gale, a sentiment echoed by others.

"People are getting a little bit concerned about just what our reporting season is going to bring, notwithstanding the decrease in interest rates yesterday," said Peake Lands Kirwan broker Kevin Lourey.

Among individual stocks, Aristocrat Leisure resumed trade after a week-long suspension and plunged 37 cents to A$2.50 before recovering to close 22 cents down at A$2.65 amid concerns over its Colorado licence renewal refusal.
